previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of end-stage renal disease, polycystic kidney disease, atrial fibrillation, and recurrent bacteremia presented from dialysis with rigors and a temperature of 100°F. She reported persistent fatigue, malaise, and chronic back pain since completing a course of cefazolin for Klebsiella bacteremia 10 days prior. She had recent dental work and took an unknown prophylactic antibiotic. Initial labs showed stable leukocyte count, elevated calcium at 11.0 mg/dL, and subtherapeutic INR of 1.3. A chest X-ray revealed small bilateral pleural effusions and mild pulmonary congestion without pneumonia. She was started on empiric vancomycin and cefepime. Blood cultures and CMV viral load were negative. Given lack of ongoing symptoms, absence of infection markers, and no growth in cultures, antibiotics were discontinued. Her hypercalcemia was managed with continuation of cinacalcet and sevelamer, holding vitamin D, and using a low-calcium dialysis bath. Warfarin was adjusted to improve INR, which rose to 1.6. She remained clinically stable, afebrile, and was discharged home with plans for outpatient follow-up and monitoring of pending SPEP and calcium levels.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ with complex medical history now with ESRD on HD, recurrent 
fevers with bacteremia in the past, c. diff diagnosed ___ on 
PO vancomycin now presenting with increased diarrhea x6 days 
concerning for relapsed c. diff.

# Diarrhea: Stool positive for c. diff on ___, did respond to 
PO vancomycin although diarrhea recurred with resuming diet per 
pt. Per pt and OMR review, pt reported formed stools with mild 
persistent cramping on ___ course of vancomycin was 
extended by four days, and pt taking on day of return to ED. 
Denies fevers/chills at home, mild abdominal cramping without 
significant pain. No N/V or known sick contacts to suggest viral 
gastroenteritis. Repeat C. diff negative, along with and stool 
cultures.  Low suspicion for norovirus given absence of N/V, 
overall feeling well except for diarrhea.  Patient only had one 
other episode of loose stool during admission without other 
symptoms, and was tolerating a lactose free diet without 
difficulty.  Despite negative C. diff result, decision was made 
to continue vancomycin for two additional weeks, including a 
taper.  She will also start to taper her omeprazole over the 
next few weeks, and if tolerating without worsening dyspepsia, 
will discontinue.  Tapering PPI may help to prevent recurrent 
episodes of C. diff.

# ESRD on HD MWF: near dry weight (anywhere from ___ kg).  
Continued home sevelamer, nephrocaps, and cinicalcet, on 
midodrine on HD days.  Noted to be hyperparathyroid and 
hypercalcemic.  SPEP negative last month.  Outpatient 
neprhologist will need to titrate cinicalcet.

# Atrial fibrilliation: She is s/p modified ablation procedure. 
INR supratherapeutic on admission without evidence of active 
bleeding. Hct stable from prior. Continued home metoprolol and 
digoxin. Warfarin restarted on day of discharge with INR 2.9, 
with repeat INR this week through PCP.
